speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I hear you have fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To determine the cause, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits, appetite, or stool appearance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the severity of your symptoms. Given the "drenching" nature of the night sweats and significant weight loss, have you noticed any blood in your stool, or do you experience pain specifically in the right upper or lower quadrants?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gastric Lymphoma (Stomach Cancer).

The combination of constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), abdominal pain, and a fixed, painless supraclavicular mass (Virchow's node) strongly suggests a malignancy of the gastrointestinal tract, specifically gastric lymphoma. I will now request relevant imaging to confirm the extent of the disease.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT, Chest_CXR
